contradictions.detail: The write-up says the washer fluid pump and central locking 'do not work'. The seller's later comment says the stalk washers work, only the high-pressure washer fails, and central locking works except intermittently from the driver's door.

critical_evidence.evidence: The listing states the timing belt, tensioner and water pump were replaced in 2022, under 7,500 miles ago. Rollers, mileage, shop name and invoice are not shown here. The belt is about 4 years old, near the specialist 4–5 year interval.
No end-play measurement is mentioned. The 5-speed carries lower thrust-bearing risk, but a reading is still required.

Seller states the emissions pump and equipment have been removed. As listed, the car cannot pass a California visual smog inspection. Whether the catalytic converters and EVAP system are present is not stated.
The fuel pump was replaced in 2021. No valley fuel line, injector hose or fuel damper hose work is mentioned. Completion of the 1990 fuel rail hose recall (90V061000) is not established.

No footwell or CE panel photos are among those examined here. Disclosed faults are dead seat heaters, a non-spraying high-pressure washer, intermittent driver-door central locking and a hatch release that does not open. These are classic CE panel and ground symptoms.

documentation.rationale: Both halves are present: VIN, clean Carfax, Montana title claim and long service history with mileage-bearing invoices quoted by the seller. Paint-depth readings and videos are also referenced. They are incomplete: the 2022 belt invoice is not shown here, true mileage is unknown, and the 1995 body shop invoice has no description. There is no valley hose, CE panel or crank end-play evidence.

condition.rationale: Several faults are stated: a rack that groans when cold (internal seal wear suspected), valve cover seepage, removed emissions equipment, multiple electrical faults, a cracked dash and paint cracks and chips. Offsetting items are all claimed rather than shown: belt and water pump in 2022, fuel pump in 2021, power steering pump and lines in 2025, oil pan gasket and motor mounts in 2024. The car is also on modern PS4S tires.

price_value.rationale: No fair-value estimate or comps are supplied. The current bid of $16,380 will rise, and a no-reserve 5-speed S4 with 912 watchers plausibly lands in the mid-$20k to low-$30k range. Even if it hammers below sorted-car money, the established work (rack, emissions restoration, valve covers, electrics) plus 928 catch-up pulls risk-adjusted value down.

mission_fit.rationale: It has the required manual and a strong point of view, and 5-speed S4s resell readily. However, it is a 39-year-old 928 with known electrical and steering faults, an unknown true mileage and a California smog problem. That is weak on the 'reliable, inspectable bridge' brief, and the likely hammer sits above the ideal band.

logistics.rationale: The car is in Missoula, MT, roughly 1,000 miles from Carmel. It is a timed BaT auction closing in about 2.5 days, and PPI access is not stated. California registration is not feasible until the air injection equipment is restored and the car passes smog. BaT Verified Checkout and shipping are available.

emotional_spec_fit.rationale: A 5-speed S4 in Grand Prix White over Cobalt Blue is genuinely desirable. This is offset by Panamera wheels, an aftermarket stereo and a polished ball shift knob, although the original phone-dial wheels and shift knob come with the car.

Have the engine valley fuel lines, injector hoses and fuel damper hoses ever been replaced? Is there a receipt, or a record of the 1990 fuel rail hose recall (90V061000) being done?
Exactly which emissions components were removed (air pump, diverter valve, check valves, lines, catalytic converters, EVAP)? Do any of the removed parts come with the car?

Is there any record of the clutch being replaced, and at what mileage? Does it slip in 4th or 5th under full throttle, and where does it engage?
Is there any drone or whir that changes with engine rpm rather than road speed, around 2,000–3,000 rpm?
What are the DOT date codes on the four Pilot Sport 4S tires?
When was the radiator last replaced? Can you photograph the expansion tank and the coolant and oil filler caps for any milkiness?
Does the 1995 Elite Auto Body invoice name the panels or parts replaced? Can you photograph the front frame rails and the inner fender seams from underneath?
Would you allow an independent 928-knowledgeable inspector in Missoula, including a crank end-play measurement, before the auction ends?
Has the car been checked for stored faults or a warning light on the central warning panel? Do all the gauges read correctly?
ppi_focus: Crank end play with a dial indicator, even on the 5-speed.
Timing belt tension, tensioner pivot and cam gear wear, cross-checked against the 2022 invoice.
Engine valley: raw fuel smell after a hot shutdown, condition of the visible fuel and injector hoses, fuel rail hose recall part.
Steering rack: fluid on the boots and crossmember; confirm the cold groan comes from internal seals.
Inventory of the emissions system (air pump, cats, EVAP) and a quote to restore it for California smog.
Clutch slip and engagement height, clutch hydraulics for leaks, torque tube bearing noise.
CE panel, footwell carpet, cowl and sunroof drains, battery tray and grounds; diagnose the seat heater, locking and hatch faults.
Front structure for evidence of the 1995 repair: frame rails, core support, inner fenders, panel gaps, paint depth.
Cooling system: radiator end tanks, internal coolers for oil/coolant cross-contamination, expansion tank, hoses.
Valve cover seepage, cam seal and rear main areas; tire date codes; surface rust on the front subframe and brackets.
what_would_change_verdict: Up: the 2022 belt invoice, valley hose receipts and footwell/CE panel photos posted, plus a Missoula PPI with good crank end play and a healthy clutch before the close.
Up: confirmation that the catalytic converters and EVAP are intact and only the air pump system needs restoring, with a firm quote.
Down: evidence that the 1995 repair was structural, crank end play near the 0.4 mm limit, clutch slip, or water damage to the CE panel or harness.
Down: the hammer runs well into the $30k range once known work and catch-up are considered.
evidence.mission_note: It meets the manual requirement and has real character, and 5-speed S4s resell well. As a reliable, inspectable bridge it is weak: a remote, short-fuse auction car with known steering, electrical and California smog work, an unknown true mileage, and a likely hammer above the ideal band.
evidence.rationale: The listing establishes a VIN-consistent 1987 928 S4 with a photo-confirmed 5-speed. It claims a clean Montana title and has a clean Carfax. Its mileage trail is coherent but explicitly unknown in total, because the odometer gear was repaired at 112,620 in 2021. Recent work is claimed (belt, tensioner and water pump in 2022; fuel pump; power steering pump and lines; oil pan gasket and mounts), and a records file is referenced, but no individual invoice is examined here. Several items are observed wrong by the seller's own disclosure: removed emissions equipment, which blocks California smog as listed; a cold-groaning steering rack; valve cover seepage; multiple electrical faults suggesting CE panel or ground trouble; a cracked dash and paint defects. A 1995 body shop invoice of about $12,650 has no description, so whether that repair was structural remains open despite the seller's 2021 mechanic check and paint-depth readings. Crank end play, valley fuel hoses and the recall, clutch and torque tube condition, and the cooling system are all undocumented. The seller is notably forthcoming, which improves the chance of getting answers before the close.
evidence.next_action: Before Monday's close, ask the seller to post the 2022 timing belt invoice, footwell/CE panel photos and an itemised list of the removed emissions parts. In parallel, book a 928-knowledgeable inspector in Missoula for a crank end-play and clutch check.
